signals.observation: ὀρθῶς appears in Socrates' statement about the correctness of founding the city and returns as agreement from the interlocutor regarding the necessity that prevents multiple Forms of bed.

signals.observation: Forms of μίμησις, μιμητής, and μιμητικός recur throughout, beginning with the exclusion of mimetic poetry, moving through the question of what mimesis is, identifying the painter as imitator, and concluding with the inability to distinguish imitation from knowledge.

elements.context: περὶ ποιήσεως λέγω

signals.observation: Forms of ποίησις and ποιητής move from poetry and tragic poets through a maker of all things, to making with a mirror, to god as true maker of the bed, and finally to the painter who is denied the title ποιητής.

elements.context: τὸ μηδαμῇ παραδέχεσθαι αὐτῆς ὅση μιμητική
παντὸς γὰρ μᾶλλον οὐ παραδεκτέα νῦν

signals.observation: The infinitive παραδέχεσθαι naming the exclusion of mimetic poetry is immediately echoed by the verbal adjective παραδεκτέα stating that it must not be admitted.

signals.observation: Forms of φαίνω recur in contrast to being, first stating that something appears more clearly, then contrasting what appears with what truly is, appearing versus differing in reality, and appearance as the object of painting.

elements.context: φαινόμενα, οὐ μέντοι ὄντα γέ που τῇ ἀληθείᾳ

πρὸς τὸ ὄν, ὡς ἔχει, μιμήσασθαι

signals.observation: Participial forms of εἰμί recur as the standard against which appearance and imitation are measured: what appears is not truly being, the craftsman does not make what is, his work is dim compared to truth, god wants to be truly a maker of what truly is, and painting imitates what appears rather than what is.

elements.context: λώβη ἔοικεν εἶναι πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα τῆς τῶν ἀκουόντων διανοίας

signals.observation: λώβη names mimetic works as harm or corruption to the thought of listeners who lack the antidote of knowledge.

elements.context: ὅσοι μὴ ἔχουσι φάρμακον τὸ εἰδέναι αὐτὰ οἷα τυγχάνει ὄντα

signals.observation: φάρμακον names knowledge of what things truly are as an antidote to the harm of mimetic works.

elements.context: φιλία γέ τίς με καὶ αἰδὼς ἐκ παιδὸς ἔχουσα περὶ Ὁμήρου

signals.observation: φιλία names Socrates' affection and reverence for Homer from childhood; φίλε later addresses the interlocutor.

elements.context: φιλία γέ τίς με καὶ αἰδὼς ἐκ παιδὸς ἔχουσα περὶ Ὁμήρου

signals.observation: Ὁμήρου is named as the object of Socrates' childhood affection and reverence, described as the first teacher and guide of all beautiful tragic works, yet honored below truth.

elements.context: οὐ γὰρ πρό γε τῆς ἀληθείας τιμητέος ἀνήρ

πόρρω ἄρα που τοῦ ἀληθοῦς ἡ μιμητική ἐστιν

signals.observation: Forms of ἀλήθεια recur: Homer is honored below truth, the craftsman's work is dim compared to truth, the tragedian is third from truth, things appear but are not truly being, painting is imitation of appearance not truth, and imitation is far from the true.

elements.context: ὁ δημιουργὸς ἑκατέρου τοῦ σκεύους πρὸς τὴν ἰδέαν βλέπων
πολλά τοι ὀξύτερον βλεπόντων

signals.observation: Forms of βλέπω occur as the sharper seeing of those who may see before duller ones and as the craftsman's looking toward the Form while making.

signals.observation: Forms of εἶδος and ἰδέα move from parts of the soul, through the customary positing of one Form for each many, to two Ideas for bed and table, to the craftsman looking toward the Idea, to three overseers of three kinds of beds, to the Form that would appear if god made two, and finally to εἴδωλον as what the painter touches and produces.

signals.observation: Forms of κλίνη recur with high local density, moving from many beds to one Form of bed, to the craftsman making beds by looking toward the Form, to three kinds of beds, to god making one bed in nature, to the question of what the painter is in relation to the bed, and to viewing the bed from different angles.

signals.observation: Forms of δημιουργός recur through the craftsman of implements looking toward the Form, a maker of all things, quick making with a mirror, such makers including the painter, the carpenter as craftsman, the painter denied the title, the painter as imitator of what craftsmen make, and knowledge of all crafts.

elements.context: τρίτος τις ἀπὸ βασιλέως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας πεφυκώς
τὸν τοῦ τρίτου ἄρα γεννήματος ἀπὸ τῆς φύσεως

signals.observation: τρίτος appears twice in close succession: the tragedian is third by nature from king and truth, and the imitator is named as third generation from nature.

elements.context: τριτταί τινες κλῖναι αὗται γίγνονται

ναὶ τρεῖς
τρίτος τις ἀπὸ βασιλέως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας
τὸν τοῦ τρίτου ἄρα γεννήματος

signals.observation: Forms of three recur: three kinds of beds come to be, three overseers of three forms of beds (painter, carpenter, god), and the imitator as third from nature and truth.

elements.context: ἣν φαῖμεν ἄν, ὡς ἐγᾦμαι, θεὸν ἐργάσασθαι
ζωγράφος δή, κλινοποιός, θεός
οὔτε ἐφυτεύθησαν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ
ταῦτα δὴ οἶμαι εἰδὼς ὁ θεός

signals.observation: θεός is named as the maker of the bed in nature, listed with painter and carpenter as three overseers, and identified as the one who planted only one Form and who knew these things.

elements.context: τρίτος τις ἀπὸ βασιλέως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας πεφυκώς

signals.observation: βασιλέως appears as the point from which the tragedian is third by nature, paired with truth.

elements.context: εἰ ʼθέλεις λαβὼν κάτοπτρον περιφέρειν πανταχῇ

signals.observation: κάτοπτρον names the mirror by which one can quickly make appearances of sun, earth, living things, implements, and plants by carrying it everywhere.

signals.observation: Forms of ζωγράφος and related painting terms recur: the painter is among such makers, makes a bed in a certain way, makes one of three beds, is denied the title of craftsman and maker, imitates craftsmen's works, will paint shoemaker and carpenter, and if skilled can deceive children and foolish people.

signals.observation: Forms of φύσις and φύω recur: the bed in nature, god making one bed in nature, god causing it to grow by nature, the name φυτουργός for god, god making all things by nature, the imitator as third generation from nature, the tragedian by nature third from truth, and the question whether the painter imitates each thing itself in nature.

elements.context: τρεῖς οὗτοι ἐπιστάται τρισὶν εἴδεσι κλινῶν
πάσας ἐπισταμένῳ τὰς δημιουργίας
οὐδὲν ὅτι οὐχὶ ἀκριβέστερον ὁτουοῦν ἐπισταμένῳ

signals.observation: Forms of ἐπιστάτης, ἐπίσταμαι, and ἐπιστήμη recur: three overseers of three forms of beds, someone knowing all crafts, knowing anything more precisely than anyone, and the triad of knowledge, lack of knowledge, and imitation that one must be able to examine.

elements.context: ἐντυχὼν γόητί τινι καὶ μιμητῇ

signals.observation: γόητί names the sorcerer or charlatan encountered alongside the imitator, who deceives the naive person into thinking he possesses all wisdom.

elements.context: πόρρωθεν ἐπιδεικνὺς ἐξαπατῷ ἂν τῷ δοκεῖν
ἐντυχὼν γόητί τινι καὶ μιμητῇ ἐξηπατήθη

signals.observation: Forms of ἐξαπατάω name deception: the painter deceiving from a distance by seeming to be a true carpenter, and the naive person deceived by encountering a sorcerer and imitator.

elements.context: παῖδάς γε καὶ ἄφρονας ἀνθρώπους
φιλία γέ τίς με καὶ αἰδὼς ἐκ παιδὸς ἔχουσα

signals.observation: Forms of παῖς occur as children whom the painter can deceive and as Socrates' affection from childhood for Homer.

elements.context: πόρρω ἄρα που τοῦ ἀληθοῦς ἡ μιμητική ἐστιν
πόρρωθεν ἐπιδεικνὺς ἐξαπατῷ ἂν

signals.observation: Forms of πόρρω name distance: imitation is far from the true, and the painter deceives by showing from a distance.

elements.context: τοὺς τῆς τραγῳδίας ποιητὰς
τῶν καλῶν ἁπάντων τούτων τῶν τραγικῶν
τοῦτʼ ἄρα ἔσται καὶ ὁ τραγῳδοποιός

signals.observation: Forms naming tragedy recur: poets of tragedy, all these beautiful tragic works for which Homer is first teacher, and the tragedian as third from truth.

elements.context: ἐάντε ἐκ πλαγίου αὐτὴν θεᾷ ἐάντε καταντικρὺ

signals.observation: θεᾷ names viewing the bed from the side or straight on as an example of how the same thing appears different without differing.

elements.context: φαντάσματος ἢ ἀληθείας οὖσα μίμησις

signals.observation: φάντασμα names appearance or semblance as the object of painting's imitation, contrasted with truth.

elements.context: ζωγραφήσει ἡμῖν σκυτοτόμον, τέκτονα
ζωγραφήσει ἡμῖν σκυτοτόμον, τέκτονα
γράψας ἂν τέκτονα καὶ πόρρωθεν ἐπιδεικνὺς
ὡς ἀληθῶς τέκτονα εἶναι

signals.observation: The painter will paint a shoemaker and carpenter without understanding their crafts, yet can deceive children and foolish people from a distance into thinking the painted carpenter is truly a carpenter.
